recommendation: Pursue cached certificates with incremental publication and measured publication cadence; this experiment supports moving historical replay off the opening path, not eliminating its cost.
mechanism: Each member independently admits its received messages and derives the proposed causally closed cut before signing context, coverage root, summary hash and canonical frontier.
Three distinct pinned endorsements from a fixed four-member roster authorize a cached certificate. Opening requires no new endorsements.
Content-addressed filesystem certificates support fallback when the latest published blob is physically removed, followed by authenticated tail admission.

Membership proofs under the final post-tail coverage root preserve every known local frontier head before atomic installation. Successful warm rebase retains previously supplied signed bodies without refolding them.
Explicit candidate, certificate, tail-step and serialized-tail-byte budgets limit fallback work. Unix cache reads reject symlinks and non-regular files without FIFO blocking.

validation.mutation_evidence: All 8 deliberate regressions killed by executed failing tests; cached-mutation-results.json
validation.oracle: Every benchmark scenario checks installed state against full real-core replay outside the timed interval.

measurement_scope: Three local repetitions; certificate filesystem read/decode, verification and already-typed tail admission. Tail decoding, pinned public context, offer construction, rendering and oracle assertions excluded. Publication separately measured. Logical cold clients, not OS-cold storage, browser or network measurements.
limits: Experimental code only; production cbcl-core is unchanged.
Correctness relies on the pinned endorsement policy and honest independent verification, not a succinct proof of computation.
A local floor prevents losing known history; a fresh client cannot infer globally newest state from an old valid certificate.
Member reconstruction and endorsement currently rebuild full accepted cuts. Incremental roots and summaries are the next implementation question.
Cadence and availability determine residual tail costs. Budget exhaustion can refuse an otherwise valid long catchup.
Frontiers, provider archives and retained signed evidence can grow. This is not a secure garbage-collection or bounded-storage result.
Fixed four-member roster, f=1; reconfiguration and general-kernel resource counters remain outside scope.
Unix-specific file hardening is tested; no universal I/O deadline or production crash-durability claim.
